{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f0b244b660ce1faf2433b1fb1f442b90913642dcca6550dda2e6526007ea5edc","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Turning, intersections and roundabouts","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Turning, intersections and roundabouts","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Turning, intersections and roundabouts

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A38
Before a turn, scan every corner for controls, pedestrians and vehicles, and signal the intended movement. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A38
Enter and hold the lane position nearest the intended turn direction. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A38
Look as far along the intended turning path as possible. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A38
After turning, accelerate smoothly to an appropriate speed, confirm the signal has cancelled and check behind. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A38
Start a right turn from the lane’s rightmost portion without first swinging left. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A38
Start a left turn from the lane’s leftmost portion and yield to oncoming traffic. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A38
Where several lanes turn, choose the turn lane beforehand and remain in it until the turn is finished. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A38
A two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction when going around the block is impractical or impossible. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A38
Begin a reverse two-point turnabout with a right signal, a stop and side-and-rear traffic checks. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A38
For that reverse turnabout, back until the rear bumper reaches the driveway’s near edge, then back slowly while steering fully right. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A38
As the vehicle enters the driveway during the reverse turnabout, straighten the wheels and stop. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A38
Finish the reverse turnabout by selecting Drive, checking both directions and, when clear, signaling and turning left into the proper lane. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A38
Begin a forward two-point turnabout by checking mirrors, signaling left and approaching near the road center before entering the driveway or alley near its right side. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A38
In that forward turnabout, stop when the rear clears the curb or driveway edge, then check every direction, signal right and select Reverse. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A38
With the path clear, reverse slowly while steering fully right; on entering the nearest lane, straighten, stop, select Drive, cancel the right signal and proceed. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A38
Use a three-point turnabout only on a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn when going around the block is impossible. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A38
Begin a three-point turnabout by checking mirrors, signaling right and stopping along the road’s right side. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A38
For its first crossing, signal left, check traffic and the left blind spot, then turn sharply left across the road and stop only when traffic is clear. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A38
For the reversing stage, select Reverse, check traffic and both blind spots, then turn sharply right and stop on the opposite side when clear. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A38
For the final stage, select Drive, signal left, check traffic and blind spots, then turn left into the right-hand lane in the new direction when clear. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A38
After completing the three-point turnabout, check traffic, confirm signal cancellation and continue straight in the new direction. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A39
A U-turn reverses travel direction in a single smooth U-shaped movement within the road. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A39
Do not U-turn at a police-controlled intersection unless the officer directs it. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A39
Midblock U-turns are prohibited on a business-district street or a residential through highway, except at a legal opening or crossover on a divided road. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A39
Do not make a U-turn where a sign prohibits it. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A39
On an undivided highway near a curve or hillcrest, do not U-turn where an approaching driver in any direction cannot see the vehicle from 500 feet away. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A39
Do not U-turn when the maneuver cannot be completed safely without interfering with traffic. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A39
At intersections, reduce speed and scan controls, opposing and crossing traffic, pedestrians, bicycles, road conditions and limited-view areas. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A39
Do not assume other road users will obey signs or signals or yield; be ready to avoid a crash. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A39
Before entering after an intersection stop, check crossing traffic and bicycles, using the recommended left-right-left scan. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A39
A green light is not a reason to start immediately without checking that crossing traffic has cleared. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A39
Choose a gap large enough to cross, reach the proper turn lane and accelerate without assuming another driver will make room. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A39
Do not enter merely because an approaching driver signals a turn; that driver may turn farther ahead or have left the signal on. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A39
Roundabout traffic circulates one way counterclockwise. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A39
The handbook reports approximate roundabout crash reductions of 90 percent for fatalities, 75 percent for injuries and 35 percent overall compared with other intersection controls. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A39
A truck apron is the paved inner roundabout area for large trucks’ rear wheels during turns, and cars, SUVs and pickups must not use it. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0039]

Misconceptions: An approaching vehicle’s turn signal is not a safe-gap guarantee; do not stop inside a roundabout for an emergency vehicle when the source directs exiting first; truck aprons are not for cars.
Mnemonics: Use observe, position, gap and path as an authored maneuver cue.
Glossary: A turnabout reverses direction; a truck apron is the inner paved area for large-truck rear wheels; weaving occurs when entering and exiting traffic share a short section.
Dynamic facts: Signs, lane assignments and interchange control vary by location; diagrams are not a verified current road map.
